paper_id: Zhang et al. - 2019 - Cloak of Invisibility Privacy-Friendly Photo Capturing and Sharing System
title: Cloak Of Invisibility: Privacy-friendly Photo Capturing and Sharing System
motivation: Secretive photographing without consent raises privacy concerns; existing solutions are broad-brush and blunt (banning devices entirely).
problem_framing: Three privacy threats (visual, feature, inference) must be addressed; users need to express privacy without visible tags; matching must be accurate, efficient, and privacy-preserving.
key_insight: Dimension-order-independent property of vector distance enables encryption-free privacy-preserving matching; graph representation is robust to pose changes.
method_signature: Graph-based portrait profiles with voting-based graph matching; scrambled vectors + LSH for privacy-preserving distance computation.
evaluation_criteria: Matching accuracy; computation/communication cost vs Paillier encryption (0.5s+1.8s vs 0.01s per pair).
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Accuracy depends on people detection; same clothes and no face capture still challenging; vulnerable to DoS attacks with fake portrait uploads.
evidence_for_taste: cannot be directly applied in this work
thinking_moves: 把 portrait matching 转成 graph matching 问题
利用 vector distance 的 dimension-order-independent 性质绕过加密
把计算负载外包到云端同时保证隐私
先做 node-level 过滤，再做 neighbor-level 投票
分层解决 visual/feature/inference 三个层面的隐私威胁
